## Product-source finding and scope

- A target shell stops itself using `kill -STOP $$`, after `setsid`/optional original-user credentials, before `exec`. Tracing is started prior to a delayed `SIGCONT` and a bounded stream drain follows normal exit.
- Three post-spawn pre-resume fallible calls (`prepare_process_seeds`, `build_trace_agent_with_view`, optional `start_web_server_if_enabled`) can early-return without explicit child cleanup, while later `agent.run` or `SIGCONT` failures call `stop_child`. Tokio Child is not kill-on-drop by default; this is a source-supported possible stopped-shell leak, **not** a runtime-reproduced incident. Recommend an upstream guarded cleanup fix separately; do not pretend it was implemented in the website repository.
- One coherent rendered outcome: new technical article, Blog index, sitemap, and today's public-safe daily/status evidence. No workflows, protected controls, raw analytics, credentials, unrelated routes or schedule changes. Representative unchanged routes: homepage, process-exit article, prior monitor CPU article. Rollback: `72384093a88f55ffb3bdc29530926f1f57fcb96d`.
